lines.text: What if the Earth suddenly stopped spinning?
Right now, if you live near the equator, you're spinning at about a thousand miles per hour. You just don't feel it.
If the Earth stopped in an instant, you wouldn't. You'd keep flying east at a thousand miles per hour. So would cars, houses, trees, and the oceans.
Winds faster than the speed of sound would sweep across the whole planet.
But say it stopped slowly, and we survived. The oceans would slide toward the North and South Poles.
And a giant new continent would rise out of the sea, all the way around the middle of the world.
A single day would last a whole year. Six months of burning sunlight, then six months of freezing night.
So, which side would you live on? Day, or night?
